title: Shape Spironolactone Atlas
question: Choose the direction that best supports a 60-second evidence story, then deeper exploration. These are planning mockups, not the built website.

options.label: Journal Club Evidence Table
options.lineage: Clinical journal-club comparison tables, expanded into an editorial reading surface
options.thesis: Every important number sits beside what it means and what it cannot establish.
options.viewport: An asymmetric title and one large, source-annotated evidence table introduce reports, reaction mentions and missing indication data; a chapter spine leads into the story.
options.risk: The opening could feel too academic unless one clear takeaway leads the table.

raised.raise: Data density becomes intentional, with exact quantities and readable source annotations rather than decorative numbers.
A persistent chapter marker preserves the reader's place and makes deeper material easy to revisit.
A decisive headline-to-annotation scale contrast gives the first viewport one unmistakable focus.
Every interactive state has an explicit text or shape cue, never colour alone.
Missing information occupies visible, measured space instead of being hidden in a footnote.

options.label: Grand Rounds Projection
options.lineage: The annotated projection in a clinical teaching session
options.thesis: One large explanatory figure carries the first lesson before the reader opens the detail.
options.viewport: The title sits beside a commanding, correctly labelled reaction-term figure; a short annotation explains the reporting denominator and a clear link begins the story.
options.risk: The familiar editorial-science composition is effective but less distinctive than the evidence-table direction.

options.label: Evidence in Proportion
options.lineage: Bauhaus foundation-course point, line and plane, adapted to the PRD's ink/coral/teal roles
options.thesis: Measured geometric space makes the difference between recorded information and uncertainty immediately legible.
options.viewport: A dominant 52.2% figure and a precisely labelled two-part area introduce missing indication information, with product title, reading action and source beside it.
options.case: Competitive on product clarity through quantitative space; the journal-club direction has stronger identification with pharmacy peers and evaluators.
options.risk: Can feel abstract or poster-like if the reading sequence and source labels become secondary to the geometry.

options.label: Data-sublime Field
options.lineage: Dense barcode and numerical data-art fields
options.thesis: Report records resolve from a dense field into selected evidence.
options.viewport: A data field resolves a selected report count into a readable observation.
options.case: Loses audience identification and first-minute comprehension against the evidence table; pure monochrome and strobing also conflict with the stated brief and motion constraints.
options.kept: Its commitment to quantitative density and exact annotations raises the evidence table without copying the barcode costume.
options.risk: Could imply a live diagnostic instrument or overwhelm the explanatory text.

options.label: Cutting-bench Select Rail
options.lineage: Film-editing rails and visible selected/deferred frames
options.thesis: The evidence story is a sequence of inspectable frames.
options.viewport: A horizontal sequence carries the reader between evidence frames and source notes.
options.case: Loses both axes: film-editing semantics are foreign to the audience and obscure a plain evidence-reading task.
options.kept: A durable reading-position marker and reachable chapter history, translated into the table's own wayfinding.
options.risk: Horizontal scrubbing could turn reading into an unfamiliar operation.

options.label: Bitmap Type Specimen
options.thesis: Scale changes reveal the relationship between headline and evidence detail.
options.viewport: A repeated headline changes scale as the reader reaches the supporting evidence.
options.case: Loses both axes: the type experiment takes attention from the medical evidence and weakens the requested calm, precise reading.
options.kept: A strong, deliberate difference between narrative display and compact evidence annotations.
options.risk: Novel lettering can make clinical terminology harder to read.

options.label: Industrial Label Grammar
options.lineage: Quoted industrial labels and explicit physical state marks
options.thesis: Every region and state names exactly what it contains.
options.viewport: Literal label plates divide the story into named operational zones.
options.case: Loses both axes: hazard-led branding mis-signals risk and the fashion reference distracts from source interpretation.
options.kept: Explicit text and shape cues for selected, unavailable and expanded states.
options.risk: Warnings could become a decorative brand device.

options.label: Cloud Quarry
options.lineage: Surreal cut blocks of weather and visible voids
options.thesis: Known observations have mass while absent information remains a visible gap.
options.viewport: Sections reveal measured gaps between blocks of evidence.
options.case: Loses both axes: the metaphor makes missing clinical information more abstract, with little pharmacy identification and substantial performance cost.
options.kept: Missingness gets quantitatively meaningful space in the reading surface, without cloud imagery.
options.risk: Dissolving imagery could imply that uncertainty disappears.

canonCard.label: Clinical Editorial Standard
canonCard.thesis: A conventional, polished editorial page with familiar section navigation and headline statistics.
canonCard.viewport: A centered title and introductory paragraph sit above a clear statistical row, with the first chart visible below.
canonCard.risk: Familiar and easy to scan, with less distinctive interaction and composition.
